correctness.rationale: Inductively all terms are affine with coefficients in F_p[T] summing to one. The finite binary coefficient closure contains 0 and I and is invariant under T and I-T, which are injections/surjections; inverse images construct arbitrary sums, so every polynomial coefficient is term-definable. Any equation induces a homogeneous linear map with image the R-ideal B_1 V+...+B_k V; R=F_p[X]/(m_T) is principal, so this equals g(T)V. Kernel cardinality is p^{kn-rank(g(T))}, and every rank has a two-variable witness. Elementary-divisor block ranks and the irreducible-minimal-polynomial iff criterion follow. The Jordan-block family realizes all spectral sizes 2..n+1 for p>=3. Direct executable exact-matrix checks cover six diverse configurations and term equations, but are not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Supplies an exact probability invariant for every binary equation on an infinite family of finite Latin Alexander quandles, not a preselected identity. Proves all rank levels are realized by binary equations and gives complete rational canonical classification including nilpotent Jordan chains. The minimal-spectrum iff irreducible criterion is sharp; odd-characteristic Jordan models realize every possible spectral cardinality for fixed |Q|. Nine-element examples distinguish scalar from nondiagonalizable affine operations; the invariant connects a recent minimal-spectrum question to finite-module structure. It is a natural complete classification rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
